stories.headline: Landslide and flooding force evacuations in Zeballos on Vancouver Island
stories.summary: The village of Zeballos, home to about 125 people on Vancouver Island’s northwest coast, declared a state of local emergency on Friday after a landslide and flooding, CBC News reported. An evacuation order covers 22 properties, and the Strathcona Regional District said debris from a landslide had affected the area and it was unclear whether more slides were possible until a geotechnical assessment is complete. Ehattesaht First Nation Chief Simon John said a neighbour woke him around 3 a.m. as water poured into their yards, and linked the slide risk to a 2018 wildfire that damaged the slope above the village. Environment Canada warned this was the first of several wet and windy systems hitting the B.C. coast into next week.
stories.why: It is an early example of the fire-then-flood pattern that makes burned hillsides dangerous for years, and more storms are forecast for the B.C. coast.

stories.headline: MTR halts unauthorised pillar repairs at the unfinished Tung Chung West station

stories.headline: Russian missiles hit Kyiv’s power grid and a Dnipro bridge days before Abu Dhabi talks
stories.summary: Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and other regions overnight into Saturday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, damaging energy facilities, homes, a kindergarten building and the Northern (Pivnichnyi) Bridge over the Dnipro, which was temporarily closed, RFE/RL reported. Five people were injured in Kyiv, including a 14-year-old, and Mayor Vitali Klitschko called the capital’s energy supply “extremely difficult,” with parts of the city losing power, heat and water. Russia’s Defence Ministry confirmed the bridge strike, claiming it was used to move weapons. The attack comes before planned U.S.–Ukraine–Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11.

stories.deck: Several First Nations, including the St’át’imc Chiefs Council, filed federal judicial reviews seeking to overturn Ottawa’s decision to list the Alberta-to-B.C. oil pipeline as a project of national interest under the Building Canada Act.

The nations argue the listing “effectively acts as an approval” and that duty-to-consult obligations must be met before a project is listed. Chief Bonnie Adolph said her community was refused consultation because its territory is not directly on the route, despite Fraser River watershed concerns. Other applicants include Boston Bar, Cheam, Lower Nicola, Kwantlen, Kwikwetlem, Skeetchestn and Tsartlip, plus Cold Lake First Nations in Alberta. stories.headline: China readies a third market-support swap and makes buyback lending permanent
stories.deck: The PBOC said it would run another Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility operation on Tuesday, with applications topping 100 billion yuan. Share-buyback relending becomes a long-term tool and its rate falls to 1%.
stories.summary: The PBOC said it would run a third Securities, Funds and Insurance companies Swap Facility (SFISF) operation on Tuesday, with a one-year term that can be extended; 31 securities and fund firms applied for more than 100 billion yuan (about $14.9 billion), Xinhua reported. After a meeting with the financial regulator and CSRC, the central bank said it would expand participants, lower swap fees and refine collateral rules. stories.headline: Supreme Court turns down Trump administration's bid to make California set aside about 20,000 disputed mail ballots
stories.deck: On the eve of the midterms, the Supreme Court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California keep separate the mail ballots of more than 20,000 people the administration says are likely noncitizens. Lower courts had already refused.
stories.summary: On the eve of the midterms, the Supreme Court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California keep separate the mail ballots of more than 20,000 people the administration says are likely noncitizens. Lower courts had already refused. The department had sent California's secretary of state and Los Angeles County's top election official a list of about 20,000 registered voters it says are not citizens, and asked that their ballots be held back until citizenship could be verified. State and county officials questioned the list's accuracy and warned that eligible voters could be disenfranchised. On Oct 28, U.S. District Judge David Carter refused a temporary order, writing that voters must not lose a core right 'because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors'. A divided 9th Circuit panel (2-1) also refused on Friday, Oct 30. Solicitor General D. John Sauer then asked the justices on Monday morning to order the ballots kept apart, arguing that once they are mixed in 'there is no way to get the challenged ballots back'. NPR and AP reported Monday evening that the court had denied the request.
stories.why: California has more than 23 million registered voters and had received over 6 million mail ballots by Sunday, CBS News reported. The ruling means ballots are processed under the state's normal rules while the underlying lawsuit continues.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: As of our check, the Supreme Court's online docket listed only the application (filed Nov 2), not the order, and we had not seen the order's text, so we can't say whether any justices dissented. The noncitizen accusation is the administration's and has not been proven in court.

stories.summary: The People's Bank of China injected 541 billion yuan through overnight reverse repos at 1.25% on Monday, the first operation under a new framework that makes the overnight rate its main policy rate instead of the seven-day rate. Analysts quoted by Reuters said it works like a targeted 15-basis-point cut for financial institutions, though Citi called it a 'mark-to-market adjustment' and does not expect a loan prime rate cut in November.

stories.summary: Completed parallel counts by polling agencies put acting President Iliana Yotova at about 56.6% to 58.2%, against 38.6% to 40.6% for pro-Western challenger Andrey Gyurov, who conceded. Turnout was below 30%. Yotova, backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev's governing Progressive Bulgaria, opposes more arms for Ukraine and favors a negotiated peace. Official results were still pending.
stories.why: Bulgaria is an EU and NATO member on the Black Sea, and the result hands the presidency to the camp that controls the government.
stories.label: Fact (preliminary)

stories.headline: Russia detains a teenager after a U.S. warning of a 'mass casualty' threat in Moscow
stories.summary: The U.S. Embassy warned Saturday of a credible threat of a mass-casualty event at Moscow's Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, and Canada repeated the alert. Russian media reported the site was closed and evacuated. Russia's FSB said Sunday it verified the U.S. tip and detained a Russian minor who had posted TikTok photos in tactical gear with an object resembling an automatic weapon. Those details come from the FSB via state media and have not been independently confirmed.
stories.why: A similar U.S. warning came days before the 2024 Crocus City Hall attack that killed more than 140 people.
stories.label: Fact + allegation (Russian state media)

stories.headline: Rioting and looting in Frankfurt after Germany's 'Gen Z' protests; 100+ police hurt
stories.summary: Tens of thousands joined largely peaceful 'Gen Z regelt' rallies in German cities on Saturday over school funding, living costs and military conscription. In Frankfurt, rioters later damaged 17 shops and looted five, attacking police with stones, fireworks and petrol bombs. Police arrested 54 people aged 13 to 29; more than 100 officers were injured. Hesse's interior minister said most suspects were German nationals but many had immigrant backgrounds; the city's mayor said passports don't matter, only accountability. Organisers condemned the violence and plan to join Europe-wide protests on Nov 20.
stories.why: It follows riots in France last month, as a youth protest wave spreads across Europe.
stories.label: Fact + opinion

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in Gaza, including five police officers and a 4-year-old
stories.summary: A drone strike in al-Mawasi near Khan Younis killed five police officers, who Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said were on routine duty; the Israeli military said it targeted militants but gave no evidence. A separate strike in Gaza City killed three people, including a 4-year-old boy, according to hospital officials. Gaza's health ministry says about 1,580 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.
stories.why: Near-daily strikes and a stalled U.S. peace plan leave the year-old ceasefire fragile.
stories.label: Fact + allegation

stories.headline: Lamine Yamal scores twice as Barcelona thrash Alaves 6-1 to retake La Liga lead
stories.summary: Yamal and Raphinha each scored twice at Camp Nou as Barcelona bounced back from losses to PSG and Real Madrid in the past week. The win moved Hansi Flick's side two points clear of Atletico Madrid, whom they visit next Sunday; they host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday. A minute of silence was held for the 69 victims of Spain's train crash.
stories.why: Barca's title race with Atletico now heads into a head-to-head showdown.
stories.label: Fact
